title: Nested Learning: The Illusion of Deep Learning Architecture
authors: Ali Behrouz, Meisam Razaviyayn, Peilin Zhong, Vahab Mirrokni (Google; Zhong also Columbia). A version published at NeurIPS 2025.
prior_note: /home/jimmy/repos/neural-memory-study/notes/2512.24695.json (Neural Memory monograph deep-read; its mechanism facts are treated as established here and are NOT re-derived). This note settles only the STC-specific questions: which layer NL actually writes under S0 §1.6, whether the update-frequency continuum bridges W and Theta, and what CMS costs in bytes per frequency tier.

axis_verdict.S0_roster_says: S0 §3.1 files this paper as Theta-4, 'the update-frequency continuum', on the Theta-path.
axis_verdict.verdict: W-PATH. Every update the paper implements is (U-W)-shaped: it moves weight-form state at a token/chunk cadence inside a single context, and it does not change the deployed artifact. The only genuine (U-Theta) in the paper is ordinary offline continual pre-training (15B tokens) used to retrofit Llama-3 before evaluation [§9.1] — applied identically to the ICL baseline, hence a control, not the mechanism. Under S0 §2.3 the paper contains ZERO sleep-time compute: no pass runs before a query arrives, so B_s does not exist.
axis_verdict.the_finding: The paper calls itself a theory of levels spanning pre-training to attention, and the S0 roster took that self-description at face value. It is a re-parameterisation of the W layer. Theta appears in NL only as the f=0 endpoint of the frequency axis — the limit that nothing in the paper moves at test time. The continuum is a bridge in NOTATION (one axis f carries both endpoints) and not in MECHANISM (no update crosses a context boundary; no update writes back to a checkpoint).
evidence_for_the_bridge_reading: The objects CMS moves ARE the deployment weights: CMS is defined as a chain of the model's own MLP blocks, and the vanilla Transformer block is the degenerate k=1, frequency-0 case [§7.1, after Eq. 71]. In the retrofit they are literally the pre-trained Llama-3 MLP tensors: MLP_0^(f_i)(.) = MLP_pretrained_i(.) [§7.3].

The CMS objective is the TASK objective, not an inner surrogate: 'the objective of L(.) is the objective of choice for the task at hand, e.g., for language modeling it is next token prediction objective' [§7.1, after Eq. 71]. Formally that is (U-Theta)'s loss evaluated on a token chunk — the strongest single piece of evidence that the paper is writing Theta-shaped updates.

The paper asserts the identity outright: pre-training is 'one of the levels' with its own context flow, objective and optimizer, and 'the distinction of training and test time in models is the result of disconnecting the knowledge transfer process from the highest frequency level ... to the low frequency levels (i.e., pre-training)' [§6]. Box: 'No Training or Test Time in Neural Learning Modules' [§6].

Ad-hoc level stacking gives a continuous dial between the two layers: setting eta_t^(l) -> 0 'keeps the updated memory blocks close to their initial states, resulting in directly using of pre-trained blocks, without adaption' [§7.3]. A single scalar interpolates frozen-Theta and adaptive-W behaviour, which is exactly what a real bridge would look like.
evidence_against_and_why_it_decides: NO PERSISTENCE. The paper states of parametric in-context learning — its own category for these updates — 'the acquired in-context knowledge does not persist once the current context is removed' [§6, boxed claim]. In Nested CMS the block is explicitly re-initialised: 'after ceil(C^(s)/C^(s+1)) steps the value of the memory will be re-initialized to theta_0^(f_{s+1})' [§7.1, after Eq. 72]. Nothing is ever written back to the checkpoint. Under S0 §1.6 the Theta-path discriminant is that the deployment artifact changes; here it does not.

NO IDLE TIME. Every cadence in the paper is measured in TOKENS of the live sequence: C^(l) chunk sizes [§7.1 Eq. 71], and the experiments sweep 'lowest frequency' = 512 and 2K tokens [§9.1]. All updates are on-path inside the forward pass. There is no pre-query pass, so the operational definition of sleep-time compute (S0 §2.3) is unmet and (A) has no C_sleep to amortise.

THE PAPER ITSELF SCOPES OUT SLEEP. §1 sets up the two-stage neuroscience picture — rapid online (synaptic) consolidation and 'offline' (systems) consolidation that 'repeats the ... sleep spindles and slow oscillations' — and then declares: 'in this work, we focus on the first stage: memory consolidation as an online process' [§1]. The offline stage is named and declined. The paper cites the sleep-consolidation literature (Diekelmann & Born 2010; Klinzing et al.; Marshall et al. 2006; Ji & Wilson replay) as motivation for the ONLINE stage only.

THE ONE REAL (U-Theta) IS A CONTROL. The 15B-token continual pre-training in §9.1 is applied to the ICL baseline too — 'with the same process of continual pre-training with 15B tokens but without any change in the MLP blocks' [§9.1] — so it is held constant across arms and is not the contribution.
axis_verdict.how_to_write_it: In the chapter, NL belongs to the W-path as the paper that supplies the VOCABULARY the Theta-path later borrows (levels, update frequency, persistent vs adaptive knowledge storage), while itself never leaving W. Its bridge-out to the Theta-path is its own explicit exclusion [§1], not a result.

core_mechanism.note: Reduction only. The full mechanism (NSAM definitions, optimizers-as-memories, Adam/Muon reinterpretation, Hope block, M3) is already recorded in notes/2512.24695.json and is not repeated.
core_mechanism.frequency_definition: Definition 2 (Update Frequency) [§3.2]: taking one update step over one data point as the unit of time, f_A = number of updates per unit time for any component A, parametric or not. Components are ordered by f (ties broken by computational dependence) into LEVELS; higher level = lower frequency. The paper's framing claim: 'Transformer architectures are based on two extreme frequencies of update: i.e., infinity and 0 for attention and MLP blocks, respectively' [§1]. In our terms, f=infinity is the KV/attention read and f=0 is Theta; every NL contribution lives strictly between, i.e. in W.
core_mechanism.CMS_original: $$\theta^{(f_\ell)}_{i+1} = \theta^{(f_\ell)}_i - \begin{cases}\eta^{(\ell)}\sum_{t=i-C^{(\ell)}}^{i} f(\theta^{(f_\ell)}_t; x_t) & i \equiv 0 \ (\mathrm{mod}\ C^{(\ell)})\\ 0 & \text{otherwise}\end{cases}$$ [Eq. 71, §7.1], with $C^{(\ell)} := \max_i f_i \cdot C / f_\ell$ and $f(\cdot)$ the error component of an arbitrary optimizer (plain $\nabla\mathcal{L}$ in the experiments). Forward: $y_t = \mathrm{MLP}^{(f_k)}(\cdots \mathrm{MLP}^{(f_1)}(x_t))$ [Eq. 70].
core_mechanism.CMS_in_unified_notation: $$W^{(\ell)}_{i} = W^{(\ell)}_{i-1} - \eta^{(\ell)} \!\!\sum_{t=i-C^{(\ell)}}^{i}\!\! \nabla_{W}\, \mathcal{L}\big(W^{(\ell)}_{t}; x_t\big)\ \ \text{iff } i \equiv 0\ (\mathrm{mod}\ C^{(\ell)}),\qquad \text{else } W^{(\ell)}_{i}=W^{(\ell)}_{i-1} \tag{NL-1}$$ This is (U-W) with $\alpha_t = 1$ (no retention gate), $\beta_t = 1$ within a chunk and reset at the boundary (the sum IS the momentum accumulator), and — the load-bearing deviation — the OUTER loss $\mathcal{L}$ (next-token prediction) in place of the inner associative loss $\ell(W;k_t,v_t)$. Read against S0 §2.2: (NL-1) has the objective of (U-$\Theta$), the cadence and the impermanence of (U-W).
core_mechanism.self_modifying_titans_original: $$\mathcal{M}_{\square,t} = \mathcal{M}_{\square,t-1}\big(\alpha_t I - \eta_t k_t k_t^\top\big) - \eta_t \nabla \mathcal{L}\big(\mathcal{M}_{\square,t-1}; k_t, \hat v_{\square,t}\big),\quad \square \in \{k,v,q,\eta,\alpha,\mathrm{memory}\}$$ [Eq. 88, §8.1], with self-generated targets $\hat v_{\square,t} = \mathcal{M}_{\square,t-1}(v_t)$ and $k_t,v_t,\eta_t,\alpha_t$ each produced by their own memory; each $\mathcal{M}_\square(\cdot) = (\cdot) + W_{\square,1}\sigma(W_{\square,2}(\cdot))$ [Eq. 89].
core_mechanism.titans_in_unified_notation: $$W^{\square}_t = W^{\square}_{t-1}\big(\alpha_t I - \eta_t k_t k_t^\top\big) + S^{\square}_t,\qquad S^{\square}_t = -\eta_t \nabla_W\, \ell\big(W^{\square}_{t-1}; k_t, \hat v_{\square,t}\big) \tag{NL-2}$$ Three deviations from (U-W): (i) the retention gate is MATRIX-valued and data-dependent, $\alpha_t I - \eta_t k_t k_t^\top$, not the scalar $\alpha_t$ — this is the Delta-Gradient-Descent decay obtained by Sherman-Morrison for normalised inputs [§4.5, App. C]; (ii) $\eta_t$ and $\alpha_t$ are themselves outputs of W-layer memories rather than schedules; (iii) the value is self-generated from the memory's own previous state, so $\ell$ has no exogenous target.
core_mechanism.chunked_deployment_form: Both rules are executed with a stale snapshot for parallelism: all of $k_t,v_t,\hat v_{\square,t},\eta_t,\alpha_t$ and all inner gradients for chunk $\lceil t/C\rceil$ are generated from $\mathcal{M}_{\square, C\lceil t/C\rceil}$, the state at the END of the previous chunk [Eq. 90, §8.2]. Two distinct chunk sizes are used: one for $\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{memory}}$, one shared by all other memories [§8.2].
core_mechanism.hope: Hope = self-modifying Titans (small state, expressive rule) feeding the CMS chain (large capacity, simple rule); the two are described as complementary [§8.3]. Hope-Attention = softmax attention + CMS, used to isolate the CMS contribution [§7.1, §9.2].

notation_conflicts.ours: $W$ for every level above pre-training; $\Theta$ ONLY for the level-1 (pre-training) parameters
notation_conflicts.why: Hard collision. The paper's $\Theta$ denotes parameters at ANY level, including test-time-mutating CMS blocks. Writing NL's $\theta^{(f_\ell)}$ as our $\Theta$ would silently reclassify the paper onto the Theta-path. S0 §1.2 P2 forbids it.

notation_conflicts.paper: $\mathcal{L}(\cdot)$ (task objective, used at CMS cadence in Eq. 71)
notation_conflicts.why: Same symbol, same meaning — but note in the chapter that NL evaluates the OUTER loss at an INNER cadence. That is the whole ambiguity of the paper in one line.
S0 reserves lowercase $\ell$ for the inner loss; the paper's tilde is not available to us.
NM reserves $\mathcal{M}(\cdot;W)$ for the READ function. NL uses $\mathcal{M}$ for the mutable object itself. Split it when quoting Eq. 88.
Compatible with NM's $C$ = chunk. NOT $C_{\mathrm{cap}}$. S0 §1.5 collision applies: never let NL's $C^{(\ell)}$ drift into the capacity slot.
v2 forbids new cost symbols (S0 §1.2 P4) but $f$ is a cadence, not a cost. Keep $f$ as a chapter-local symbol and always state its unit as tokens: $f_\ell = 1/C^{(\ell)}$.
$\hat c$ is reserved for the E-path learned context (S0 §1.2). NL's $\hat v$ is an internal target inside a W-layer update. Confusing them would fabricate an E-path reading of this paper.
All learning rates in NL's mechanism are inner. $\eta_\Theta$ applies only to the 15B-token continual pre-training of §9.1.
Compatible; both are momentum quantities. Keep the subscript per S0 §1.5 so it never collides with $S(c;B_s)$.

notation_conflicts.ours: keep as the paper's local term
notation_conflicts.why: Do not translate 'level' into our 'layer'. Our three layers are $\Theta/W/E$; NL's levels all sit inside $W$ plus the $\Theta$ endpoint.

update_layer.instantiates: (U-W) at two nested cadences. (U-E) never. (U-Theta) exactly once, outside the mechanism.
update_layer.cadence_1_self_modifying_titans: Per token, executed per chunk $C$ against the previous chunk's snapshot [Eq. 90, §8.2]. Six memories per block move: $\mathcal{M}_k,\mathcal{M}_v,\mathcal{M}_q,\mathcal{M}_\eta,\mathcal{M}_\alpha,\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{memory}}$, each a 2-layer residual MLP [Eq. 89].
update_layer.cadence_2_CMS: Every $C^{(\ell)}$ tokens per level $\ell$ [Eq. 71]. Experiments group variants by 'lowest frequency', swept at 512 and 2K tokens [§9.1]. The slowest tier in any reported run is therefore 2K TOKENS — about one long document, not a session and not a round.
differences_from_canonical_U_W: CMS uses the TASK loss (NTP), not an associative inner loss: 'the objective of L(.) is the objective of choice for the task at hand' [§7.1]. Canonical (U-W) uses $\ell(W;k_t,v_t)$.

CMS has no retention gate ($\alpha_t \equiv 1$) and no cross-chunk momentum; retention is provided structurally instead, by keeping a slower tier whose copy of the knowledge survives [§7.1, 'CMS Design Helps with Continual Learning'].

Self-modifying Titans replaces the scalar gate with the matrix $\alpha_t I - \eta_t k_t k_t^\top$ and makes $\eta_t,\alpha_t$ themselves memory outputs [Eq. 88] — i.e. the (U-W) hyperparameters are promoted into $W$.

Targets are self-generated ($\hat v_{\square,t} = \mathcal{M}_{\square,t-1}(v_t)$), so the update is self-referential; the paper notes exact self-reference is inherently sequential and the chunked stale snapshot is the engineered compromise [§8.2].
update_layer.the_theta_event: Class-incremental experiments only: Llama3-8B / Llama-3B, MLP blocks restructured into levels via ad-hoc level stacking [§7.3], 'followed by continual pre-training with 15B tokens' [§9.1]. This is a plain (U-Theta) round — offline, gradient descent on a corpus, artifact changes — but it is one-shot, author-side, pre-evaluation, and identically applied to the ICL baseline [§9.1]. It is not on a sleep cadence and NL contributes nothing to it.
update_layer.order: No composition across layers. There is no (U-E) -> (U-Theta) sequence and no (U-W) -> (U-Theta) writeback. Within W the order per chunk is: snapshot -> generate all $k,v,\hat v,\eta,\alpha$ for the chunk -> compute all inner gradients against the snapshot -> apply at the boundary [Eq. 90, §8.2]; CMS tier $\ell$ applies at its own boundary [Eq. 71].

outer_vs_inner.object: Embeddings, norms, short convolutions (window 4), the one static projection $W_q$
Initial states $\mathcal{M}_{\square,0}$ of all six self-modifying memories
outer_vs_inner.who_learns_it: Outer / pre-training (meta-learned, MAML-form knowledge transfer by initialisation)
outer_vs_inner.when: Level 1. The paper argues a well-trained low-frequency level is what lets the high-frequency level adapt fast; without it 'the higher-frequency level is on its own to learn from the context' and may not converge on the available context [§7.3 rationale, §6].
Every chunk, against the previous chunk's snapshot.

outer_vs_inner.who_learns_it: NEITHER — generated per token by $\mathcal{M}_\eta,\mathcal{M}_\alpha$; only their generators' initial states are meta-learned
Generated, not learned — by the memory being updated, from $v_t$
outer_vs_inner.when: Per token (per chunk snapshot in practice).

outer_vs_inner.who_learns_it: BOTH — initial state outer (Sequential: all inits meta-learned at the lowest frequency, Eq. 73; Nested: level $s$ meta-learns level $s{+}1$'s init, Eq. 72), the running state inner by (NL-1)
outer_vs_inner.when: Init at pre-training; running state every $C^{(\ell)}$ tokens; in the Nested variant reset to the meta-learned init at the end of the level's context [§7.1].

outer_vs_inner.object: CMS levels in the retrofit path
outer_vs_inner.who_learns_it: Initialised from an existing pre-trained model's MLP blocks, then moved by 15B tokens of continual pre-training (outer), then by Eq. 71 at test time (inner)

outer_vs_inner.object: M3 optimizer state ($M^{(1)}$ per step, $M^{(2)}$ per $f$ steps, $V$ per step)
outer_vs_inner.who_learns_it: Neither — it is optimizer state during pre-training; CMS applied to the gradient context flow
outer_vs_inner.when: Training only. Not present at serving.

B_s.reason: There is no pre-query offline pass in this paper, so the quantity is not merely unreported — it is undefined for NL. The nearest reported figure is a WAKE-time amortised update cost: for a model with $L_{\mathrm{layer}}$ layers, 4 CMS levels with highest frequency $\hat f$ and hidden dimension $d_{\mathrm{in}}$, 'on average, the update cost is for $O(\frac{1}{\hat f}\times\frac{L_{\mathrm{layer}}}{5}\times d_{\mathrm{in}}^2)$ of parameters' [§7.1, 'Is CMS Efficient Enough?']. That is parameters touched per step during the forward pass, not a sleep budget, and it is given in parameters, not FLOPs or tokens.

L_w.reason: No latency, TTFT, ITL, throughput or wall-clock number is reported for Hope or Hope-Attention anywhere in the paper. The single efficiency measurement in the paper concerns the M3 OPTIMIZER during training: M3 is 'reletively slower compare to the Muon optimizer, and show on par efficiency with AdaMuon' at 140M and 1.3B [§9.7, Figure 12]. The only qualitative statement touching wake cost is that 'the frequency of update directly affects the efficiency of the model' and that lowest-frequency 2K 'offers significantly more efficient forward pass' than 512 [§9.1] — a comparison with no units on either side.

C_cap.reason: No byte count, parameter count, or state size for Hope's inference state appears in the paper. The one memory statement is comparative and unquantified: Cartridges is excluded from the level comparison 'mainly due to the fact that Hope has higher memory usage and there are fundamental differences in their computational costs' [§9.1]. Neither $d_{\mathrm{in}}$ nor $L_{\mathrm{layer}}$ nor the CMS level count of the reported Hope models is stated, so the paper's own $O(\frac{1}{\hat f}\frac{L_{\mathrm{layer}}}{5}d_{\mathrm{in}}^2)$ expression cannot be evaluated numerically from the paper.

rho.reason: No per-round degradation is reported. The surrogates are end-task: class-incremental accuracy on CLINC/Banking/DBpedia [§9.1, Figure 6] and CTNL ChRF where ICL 'faces dramatic performance drop' under sequential two-language learning while Hope-1/2/3 improve monotonically and Hope-3 nearly recovers the non-continual score [§9.1, Table 8/Figure 8]. The only quantified forgetting horizon in the paper is for the OPTIMIZER, not the model: with $\beta=0.9$, 'the last 6 gradients (resp. 43 gradients) are responsible for at least 50% (resp. 99%) of the cumulative contribution' [§4.3].

CMS_bytes_per_frequency_tier.reported: NO. The paper never reports bytes, per tier or in total, and never states the tier count or width of the evaluated models.
CMS_bytes_per_frequency_tier.structural_answer_marked_as_inference: [INFERENCE] A CMS tier does not add a small auxiliary state the way a KV cache or a matrix-valued fast weight does. Eq. 71 makes an existing MLP BLOCK mutable, so the per-sequence state of tier $\ell$ is the full parameter tensor of that block — $O(d\,d_{\mathrm{in}})$ per block per layer, times dtype width — and it is identical for every tier regardless of $C^{(\ell)}$. Frequency changes the WRITE TRAFFIC (one full-block write per $C^{(\ell)}$ tokens), not the capacity. Hence the cost curve across the continuum is flat in bytes and $1/C^{(\ell)}$ in bandwidth. Nothing in the paper contradicts this and nothing in the paper states it.
CMS_bytes_per_frequency_tier.why_it_matters_for_v2: This is the number the Part III cost decomposition needs and cannot get from this paper. Any bytes-per-tier figure used in the monograph must be marked as the book's own construction, not attributed to NL.

cost_table.amortisation: Equation (A) cannot be applied. $C_{\mathrm{sleep}} = 0$ because no computation precedes the query, and $N_q$ is undefined because no artifact is shared across queries — every context starts from the meta-learned initial states. Break-even $N_q^*$ does not exist for this paper.

experiments.language_modeling: From scratch on FineWeb-Edu + long-context mix, 32K vocab, AdamW: 760M/30B tokens and 1.3B/100B tokens. 760M — Hope Wiki ppl 18.68, LAMBADA ppl 20.07, avg acc 52.28 (Titans 51.68, RWKV-7 50.55). 1.3B — Wiki 14.39, LAMBADA 10.08, avg 58.04 (Titans 56.82, Samba 54.46, Transformer++ 53.38) [Table 2, §9.3].
experiments.RULER_NIAH: ~50B tokens from scratch. Hope best attention-free across S-NIAH-1/2/3 and MQ/MK/MV at 4K-16K (S-NIAH-3 16K: Hope 24.8 vs Titans 21.2, RWKV-7 5.8; MK-NIAH 16K: Hope 14.8 vs Titans 8.2). Hope-Attention beats Transformer on S-NIAH-1: 100/100/100 vs 88.6/76.4/79.8 at 4K/8K/16K [Table 1, §9.2].
experiments.BABILong: Hope (fine-tuned) stays competitive out to 10M tokens where Titans and ARMT degrade after ~1M and GPT-4-class zero-shot models fail around 128K-256K; the RAG-augmented Llama-8B also drops with context [Figure 9, §9.2].
experiments.continual_learning: Class-incremental CLINC (150 intents), Banking (77), DBpedia (70 second-level classes, 10K train / 1K test sampled). Backbones Llama3-8B and Llama-3B, MLPs restructured via ad-hoc level stacking + 15B-token continual pre-training. Hope beats ICL, EWC, and InCA (external-learner baseline) on all three [Figure 6, §9.1].
experiments.levels_and_frequency: LongHealth (20 patient documents, 5.1K-6.8K words, 200 questions), QASPER (~5K QA over ~1.6K NLP papers, full text as context), MK-NIAH. Baselines ICL (= Hope with 1 level) and DuoAttention. All Hope variants beat both; more levels help; 'the higher the lowest-frequency the lower the performance'; lowest frequency 2K is recommended as the efficiency/quality operating point against 512 [Figure 7, §9.1].
experiments.CTNL: New benchmark: MTOB (Kalamang) + Manchu learned sequentially in context, then translated to English, scored by ChRF. ICL collapses in the sequential setup; Hope-1/2/3 improve monotonically; Hope-3 almost recovers the single-language score [Table 8 / Figure 8, §9.1].
experiments.short_recall: SWDE/NQ/DROP/FDA/SQuAD/TQA: Transformers remain best (FDA 67.3 vs Hope 41.9); Hope is best attention-free [Table 3, §9.4].
experiments.formal_languages: Irie et al. (2023) construction — parity, (aa)*, (abab)*, a^n b^n, a^n b^n c^n, Shuffle-2: Hope 100.0 on all, matching LSTM and SRWM, with the stated advantage of parallelizable training [Table 5, §9.5].
experiments.ablation: Table 6 [§9.6], ppl / reasoning acc: Hope 12.24 / 58.1; w/o DGD 13.41/56.5; w/o momentum 13.58/56.9; w/o weight decay 13.71/57.2; w/o CMS 13.04/57.3; w/o inner-projection k 13.77/56.9; w/o inner-projection v 13.90/55.1; w/o inner-projection q 12.19/57.4.
experiments.optimizer: M3 vs AdamW vs Muon on ViT 24M/86M (MLP dim 1536/3072, patch 16) on ImageNet-21K (11M images, 10,450 classes): M3 best train and test loss [Figure 11, §9.7]. Training-time comparison at 140M and 1.3B: M3 slower than Muon, on par with AdaMuon [Figure 12, §9.7].

scale_ceiling: 1.3B parameters / 100B tokens for from-scratch training [Table 2, §9.3]; ~50B tokens for the RULER/BABILong runs [§9.2]; Llama3-8B (and Llama-3B) for the retrofit path, with 15B tokens of continual pre-training [§9.1]; ViT-86M / ImageNet-21K for the optimizer study [§9.7]. Nothing above 1.3B is trained from scratch, and no 7B+ Hope exists. The slowest CMS cadence ever evaluated is 2K tokens [§9.1] — that is the empirical ceiling on the 'continuum' itself, and it is three orders of magnitude short of a session, let alone a sleep round.
inherited_open_question: none-stated. The paper does not quote any predecessor's open question. Its stated points of departure are its own observations: (i) 'Transformer architectures are based on two extreme frequencies of update: i.e., infinity and 0 for attention and MLP blocks, respectively' [§1]; and (ii) that in Transformers the projections $W_k,W_v,W_q$ are optimized at the lowest-frequency level and so are frozen in context, bounding how tokens can be contextualised [§8, §8.1]. Definition 1 (associative memory) is imported wholesale from Miras [§2], and Titans supplies the deep-memory block, the meta-learned initial state and the chunkwise training procedure, but neither is cited as leaving a question NL answers. For the v2 bridge chain the honest bridge-in is therefore not a quotation but a structural one: NL takes the W-path's own design space (Miras/Titans/Atlas) and adds the frequency axis to it.
open_questions: OFFLINE CONSOLIDATION IS EXPLICITLY DEFERRED. §1 states the two-stage picture and then restricts scope: 'in this work, we focus on the first stage: memory consolidation as an online process.' This is the paper's own handoff to the sleep line and is the single most usable bridge-out in the corpus.

Catastrophic forgetting is not solved: 'the undesirable phenomenon of catastrophic forgetting is not "solved" in general ... catastrophic forgetting is a natural consequence of compression' [§10]. Capacity allocation across levels is left open.

Level design is empirical — how many levels, which frequencies, which components deserve a level. The paper offers 512 vs 2K as an efficiency judgement [§9.1], not a principle, and Table 6 shows one added level (inner $q$) hurting perplexity.

The Cartridges comparison is deferred on cost-incomparability grounds ('Hope has higher memory usage ... requiring further experiments with careful and controlled design in the future studies') [§9.1].
M3 'might suffer from computational overhead and so face challenges when scaling to larger networks' [§7.2, Figure 12].
The chunkwise stale-snapshot approximation to true self-reference gets no fidelity analysis; exact self-referential updates remain sequential [§8.2].
Serving economics of a model that gradient-updates its own MLP blocks in production — per-tenant divergence, checkpointing of the drifted state, rollback — are never raised.

unfavorable_facts.fact: Table 6's caption states 'All components of Hope are positively contributing to its performance', and Table 6 refutes it: w/o inner-projection $q$ gives ppl 12.19 against Hope's 12.24. Adding that level makes perplexity worse.

The continual-learning headline is confounded. Hope and the ICL baseline both receive 15B tokens of continual pre-training, but only Hope's backbone has its MLP blocks restructured into multiple levels; no arm isolates the restructuring from the extra adaptable parameters and extra update compute it brings. The paper attributes the gap to 'Hope's multiple levels of in-context learning' without an equal-compute or equal-parameter control.

The comparison the paper itself names as closest — Cartridges — is excluded, and the stated reason is a cost admission with no number attached: 'Hope has higher memory usage and there are fundamental differences in their computational costs'. The one place the paper concedes a resource disadvantage is also the one place it declines to measure it.

The recommended operating point is the worse-performing one. 'Lowest Frequency = 2K' is put forward as 'optimal' explicitly because it 'offers significantly more efficient forward pass', while achieving only 'close performance' with 512 — i.e. the frequency continuum is sold as a quality axis and then tuned on cost, with neither side quantified in the text.

Transformers still beat Hope decisively on short in-context recall (FDA 67.3 vs 41.9), so the 'architectures are uniform, levels are the missing axis' thesis does not translate into dominance at the regime most serving traffic occupies.

The 10M-token BABILong results are fine-tuned, not zero-shot — the figure separates fine-tuned (red) from zero-shot large-model (blue) points, and Hope is in the fine-tuned group. The long-context claim is a claim about a task-adapted model.

No wall-clock, latency, throughput or memory measurement exists for Hope. The only efficiency figure in the paper measures the M3 optimizer during training, and there M3 is SLOWER than Muon (on par with AdaMuon) — the paper's one measured efficiency result is negative for its own artifact.

'Adam is the optimal associative memory' is optimality with respect to a posited element-wise objective and a chosen target $P$ = gradient variance. It is an existence construction, not a uniqueness result, and the paper does not claim otherwise — but the framing invites the stronger reading.

The neuroscience that motivates the whole frequency argument is brain-wave frequency bands (gamma 30-150 Hz, beta 13-30 Hz, delta/theta 0.5-8 Hz) [§1] — a ratio of about 300x across the biological spectrum, all within perception-scale time. The paper transfers it to a computational spectrum whose implemented span is C^(l) from 1 token to 2K tokens, and then uses the same analogy to claim the axis reaches pre-training. The analogy is not evidence for the endpoints.

cross_path_citations.the_silence_as_finding: A paper whose stated purpose is to unify everything that updates at every timescale, published December 2025, cites zero external-memory systems and one 2017 regularisation method for the weight path. The unification is a unification of the W-path with the optimizer, dressed in vocabulary broad enough to sound like it covers all three. Per S0 §5 and STC-STYLE §0 rule 7, write this silence explicitly in the chapter's §N.8.

systems_implications: STATE IS MUTABLE WEIGHTS, PER SEQUENCE. Per Hope block the serving state is six 2-layer residual MLP memories [Eq. 89] plus the drifting CMS tiers [Eq. 71]. [INFERENCE] Shared-weight batching breaks for exactly these tensors: concurrent requests cannot share them, so each in-flight sequence needs its own copy — the Rosetta row 'batch로 weight 공유' in STC-STYLE §3 fails here even though this is a W-path paper, because the mutable object is an MLP block rather than a small matrix state.

CAPACITY IS FLAT ACROSS THE CONTINUUM, TRAFFIC IS NOT. [INFERENCE] Each CMS tier costs one full MLP block of state regardless of $C^{(\ell)}$; frequency buys write bandwidth, not bytes. A four-tier CMS therefore multiplies the per-sequence weight-state by roughly the tier count, with writes at $1/C^{(\ell)}$ per token. The paper's own amortised figure is $O(\frac{1}{\hat f}\times\frac{L_{\mathrm{layer}}}{5}\times d_{\mathrm{in}}^2)$ parameters touched per step for four levels [§7.1], which is the write-traffic side of exactly this statement — and it is stated in parameters, never in bytes, and never with $d_{\mathrm{in}}$ or $L_{\mathrm{layer}}$ supplied.

READ TRAFFIC IS FLAT IN CONTEXT LENGTH. State is $O(1)$ in $L$ rather than the KV cache's $O(L)$ [prior note; structural consequence of Eq. 71/88]. [INFERENCE] Decode latency is therefore flat in context, at the cost of six extra small-MLP forwards per block per token; the crossover against attention is visible as the short-recall deficit in Table 3 [§9.4].

PREFILL AND TRAINING PARALLELISM COME FROM STALENESS. The chunkwise scheme freezes each memory at the previous chunk boundary so all of a chunk's $k,v,\hat v,\eta,\alpha$ and all inner gradients compute in one batched pass [Eq. 90, §8.2]; inside a CMS chunk, positions with $i \not\equiv 0 \pmod{C^{(\ell)}}$ have no sequential dependence [§7.1]. Two chunk sizes are used, one for $\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{memory}}$ and one for the rest [§8.2] — a kernel-design degree of freedom, and the fidelity/throughput dial.

THE UPDATE IS GEMM-SHAPED. [INFERENCE] The deployed memories are MLPs, so the inner step is a sequence of batched small GEMMs (TTT-MLP-like), not a single scan; the linear special case $\mathcal{M}(\alpha_t I - \eta_t k_t k_t^\top) - \eta_t(\cdot)k_t^\top$ is a generalized delta rule and admits DeltaNet-style WY/UT chunk kernels.

NOTHING TO AMORTISE. [INFERENCE, grounded in the absence of any pre-query pass] Because all NL compute is on the wake path, the serving question this monograph cares about — can idle-time compute buy wake-time latency — is not asked here. NL's contribution to the v2 cost argument is negative space: it shows how far the W layer can be structured without ever leaving the request path.
